archetype.name: Play-In Team (frontcourt-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo frontcourt is good enough to keep it in the East's middle tier, but whose thin perimeter group leaves it fighting for a play-in seed rather than a guaranteed playoff spot.

report.headline: Elite frontcourt, leaky perimeter: a play-in team waiting on its defense to normalize
report.take:
Miami is 4-6 and 19th on the site, and that record is close to fair. A Net Rtg of -5.1 ranks 22nd, and the margin implies 3 wins, so the extra win from a 117-116 overtime escape in Los Angeles is the only luck in the record. The shape of the roster explains most of it. The frontcourt grades an A: Giannis Antetokounmpo sits 3rd of 85 on his tab with a +5.5 BPM on a 33.6 USG %, and Adebayo is 8th of 91 at center. The wings grade a D and the backcourt a C-. Andrew Wiggins has a 49 TS % and the team is 19 points per 100 worse with him on the floor. Tim Hardaway Jr. is 105th of 106 at shooting guard with a 39.8 TS %. The offense is fine but not good, with a 111.7 ORtg that ranks 20th. It plays fast (102.6 Pace against a 99.3 league mean), and its eFG % is slightly above the league.

The defense is the real story, and it is a strange one. Miami is excellent at keeping opponents away from the basket: Opp Rim Rate is 25.3, 4th in the league. It also ends possessions well, with DRB % 6th and Opp TOV % 7th. Yet the Opp eFG % of 58.0 is dead last, because opponents are hitting 39.4% from three, 28th. Opposing guards are doing the damage. Point guards average 31.3 points a game against Miami and shooting guards 31.6, and both groups take a bigger share of the scoring than league norms. Shooting guards also hit 5.2 threes a game, the most any defense allows. Part of that is real: this perimeter group is slow and thin. Part of it is almost certainly opponents making shots at an unsustainable rate.

History is the tiebreaker. Miami's defense ranked between 5th and 13th in each of the last five seasons, and last year's Opp 3P % was 35.9. Nothing in the profile says the scheme broke. The paint protection and defensive rebounding that usually anchor it are intact. A 25th-ranked DRtg of 116.8 should drift toward the middle of the league as the three-point luck evens out. The ceiling, though, is set by the guards and wings, not the bigs.

The early schedule was also no gift. Minnesota, Detroit, the Lakers and Golden State account for four of the six losses, and the last five games went 3-2 with a better margin than the season's. This looks like a team a bit better than a -5 net rating. It is still not a top-six team in the East unless someone on the perimeter steps up.

strengths.title: Giannis-Adebayo frontcourt carries everything
strengths.body: The frontcourt grade of A rests on two top-ten players at their positions. Antetokounmpo is producing like a star, with a +5.5 BPM and the team's highest usage. Adebayo adds a +2.1 BPM and efficient scoring. This is the most bankable part of the team and should hold all season as long as both stay healthy.

strengths.title: Paint protection and finishing possessions
strengths.body: Opponents take only 25.3% of their shots at the rim, 4th-fewest in the league. Miami grabs defensive rebounds at the 6th-best rate and forces turnovers at the 7th-best rate. These are structural traits of a defense with two elite bigs, and they are why the overall defensive numbers should improve.

strengths.title: Klay Thompson's shooting is real value
strengths.body: Thompson has hit 40 threes at a 63.8 TS %, which makes him the only efficient high-volume perimeter scorer on the roster. Pelle Larsson's 64 TS % in a low-usage role helps too. Without them the D wing grade would be worse.

concerns.title: Opponents shooting the lights out
concerns.body: The Opp eFG % of 58.0 ranks last, driven by a 39.4% opponent three-point rate. Opposing guards are scoring heavily, and shooting guards hit more threes against Miami than against any other defense. Some of this is the slow perimeter group, but a defense that keeps opponents out of the paint this well usually settles nearer last year's 35.9 Opp 3P %. Expect partial regression in Miami's favor, not a full fix.

concerns.title: Wings and guards are a minus
concerns.body: Wiggins' minutes have been costly: the team is 19 points per 100 worse with him on the floor, and he has a 49 TS %. Hardaway's 39.8 TS % and -9.7 BPM are among the worst at his position. With a D wing grade and a C- backcourt, every minute the bigs sit exposes the roster. That is the main reason the offense ranks 20th despite a decent eFG %.

concerns.title: No second chances
concerns.body: Miami's ORB % of 22.9 ranks 27th, well below the league. Its overall REB % is 25th despite strong defensive rebounding. Low offensive rebounding has been a Heat trait for years, so it is a style rather than a slump. It limits how much the offense can recover from a cold shooting night.

trend.note: A four-game losing streak to open gave way to a .500 November. The last five games went 3-2, with the margin improved over the season's. Scoring fell in November while points allowed stayed high, so the shape of the team has not changed.

weekAhead.headline: A gimme in Utah, then three home tests against winning teams
weekAhead.body:
The week opens in Utah against a 1-9 Jazz team with the league's 29th-ranked offense. That is the one game Miami should expect to win, and a chance for its shaky defense to look better against a team that can't shoot. Then come three home games in four days: Cleveland and Detroit on consecutive nights, then Houston. All three are above .500 and ranked well ahead of Miami on the site.

Detroit already beat Miami by 17 and brings the league's 2nd-best defense. Houston pairs the 3rd-best offense with the 2nd-best opponent three-point rate. Cleveland is the most beatable of the three. A 2-2 week would be a solid result; 1-3 is as likely as 3-1.

keyMatchups.title: Giannis against Houston's power-forward wall
keyMatchups.body: Houston gives up just 14.4 points a game to power forwards, and players at the position score well below their usual output against them. That is the opponent best equipped to make Antetokounmpo work for everything. Detroit, by contrast, has allowed power forwards 11.78 rebounds a game, among the most in the league, so the Pistons game is where his all-around line should flourish.

keyMatchups.title: Guard scoring at both ends
keyMatchups.body: Utah's defense gives point guards 33.5 points a game, one of the league's worst marks, so Davion Mitchell should have room to score. Detroit is the opposite: it holds point guards to 20.56 points, 3rd-fewest. Meanwhile Miami's own guards have been the soft spot of its defense all season.

keyMatchups.title: Adebayo against Cleveland's interior
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland allows centers 21.3 points a game, among the league's most, and gives up the 2nd-most rebounds to the position. That opens a clear window for Adebayo in the opener of the back-to-back.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents keep hitting threes at a 39.4% clip against Detroit and Houston. If that number starts falling, the defensive turnaround has begun.

restOfSeason.body:
The frontcourt is real and should keep Miami competitive most nights. The defense is the piece most likely to move. A team that protects the paint and finishes possessions this well has not stayed 25th in defense before, and opponent three-point shooting tends to come back toward the league average. If DRtg settles in the 113-116 range, a mid-30s to low-40s win total is the natural landing spot. The extra win from close games is minor and doesn't need to regress much.

What caps the outlook is the perimeter. With a D wing grade and a C- backcourt, Miami lacks a reliable third scorer beyond Thompson's shooting. The team depends heavily on Antetokounmpo and Adebayo staying on the floor. Expect a play-in race rather than a top-six push, with the upside tied to better wing minutes than Wiggins and Hardaway have provided.
swingFactors: Opponent 3P % regressing toward last year's level
Improvement from Wiggins and the wing rotation

confidence.note: Ten games; opponent shooting luck drives much of the defensive rating.
